title: Hashkafa
subtitle: On perspective, meaning, and the freedom to see beyond one’s own locality.
html:
From the newsletter, 1 October 2026.

Hashkafa is not idiotic. Insofar as it concerns perception and perspective, hashkafa is everything. How, then, do discussions of perspective become captured by the small-scale immaturities and inanities of judgment, predicated on the assumption that one must hold an opinion about this demographic's music, that demographic's financial habits, those people's clothes, and so on? This, too, is a meta-hashkafic reality absorbed within the realm of hashkafa itself.

These discussions rest on earlier layers of a nested hashkafic complex, a cluster of interrelated fundamental beliefs and assumptions about the world. To encounter someone concerned with which shoes to wear is to encounter someone who lives in a world of shoes, clothes, and signals, signaling and meaningful to who...?

What is meaning? Meaning assumes that information is coherent because it exists within a larger space of reality, from which it selects and in which it is contextualized. If reality is supplied by the sensitivities of the immediately surrounding community, which provides the meaning of these signals and whose eyes are the approving audience the signals are meant to find, then one's world is only as large as the locality in which those signals are meaningful. Would they be meaningful even one town over? Would they be meaningful at any other point in the history of the universe beyond this decade and this hyper-specific geographic situation?

When hashkafa is discussed, therefore, one can already tell which world is being perceived, because the questions asked are the slight gaps within an already comprehensive worldview. A language is not simply a system of references to objects. It encodes an entire way of relating to the world, including hues of perception that words can never fully capture. What might a hashkafic discussion look like among Yisrael in its freedom, blessed to be meromam mikol lashon, beyond any particular universe because it integrates all universes? Such a discussion would take place at the level of the Sanhedrin, each member of which must know all languages, must be able to speak within any world, and must generate policy for eternity that fits any possible world a Yid might inhabit until Mashiach.

It is hashkafa that opens a portal beyond the constraints of one's hyper-local world and into reality as it truly is, unmolested by the warping of a single umah and lashon.

We were mekabel the Torah only al tenai that we would be free from shlita mikol umah velashon. It is time to exercise that freedom in the pursuit of reality, which comes only through Torah. Yet this pursuit requires immense bravery. Torah is emet, and so YOU might be wrong. Are you ready to hear that you are wrong about the way you see things? That your fundamental perspectives may be alien to Torah? That Ratzon Hashem may differ from what your current lifestyle licenses and pedestals as ideal? If you are willing to question everything except the most fundamental layer of your hashkafa, you are hopeless. In the case you are wrong, you will never grow, because you possess only the illusion of dialogue in an arena of minutiae.
